narrativeReportMd:
# date R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local material breaking change was found for the `date` primitive datatype. The R6 artifact is the same canonical datatype and preserves the same primitive value regex, FHIRPath type, element set, cardinalities, modifier flags, and summary flags.

## Scope
The analysis covered the core R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions for `date`, package metadata, package index entries, and the R6 `PrimitiveType` base artifact only to classify the base-definition shift as inherited/out of scope. It did not assess date search parameters, resource-specific uses of `date`, profiles, examples, or base artifact changes as local findings.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 date instance values that satisfy the core datatype remain representable in R6, and valid R6 date primitive values are cleanly representable in R4. The main migration concern is tooling rather than data: generators that reason directly over `baseDefinition` must handle the R6 `PrimitiveType` layer, but that issue belongs to the primitive/base datatype analysis rather than to `date` itself.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no local hard, likely, or high-impact `date` findings. The changed wording from "no time zone" to "no UTC offset" and the new R6 type-characteristics metadata are notable but do not change the permitted lexical space.

## Findings requiring human review
No local findings require human review. A reviewer may still want the official R4-to-R6 diff or rendered datatype pages to confirm the intent of the editorial wording and metadata additions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The local computable constraints stayed backward-compatible. The R6 base hierarchy change appears to be a broader model cleanup and should be reviewed once for primitive datatypes generally.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the R6 `PrimitiveType`/`DataType` hierarchy and inherited Element/Extension invariant presentation in the corresponding base artifact reports.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local material breaking change was found for `date`. The value regex and FHIRPath type are unchanged, no elements were added or removed, and R6 date values remain representable in R4. The main uncertainty is limited to not having an official diff/rendered narrative to explain the non-breaking wording and metadata changes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration for `date` should mainly confirm that validators and serializers continue to use the same lexical rules for year, year-month, and full date values without offsets. Tooling that builds inheritance trees must separately account for R6 `PrimitiveType`, but that is a shared primitive/base datatype migration concern rather than a local change in `date` validation.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and package index entries are present locally and show an unchanged canonical identity, element list, cardinalities, primitive value regex, FHIRPath type, and flags. Confidence is not absolute because no official change-note diff or rendered datatype narrative was used to corroborate the intent behind the editorial wording and metadata changes.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 package contains `StructureDefinition-date.json` with the same id `date`, canonical URL, name, kind `primitive-type`, type `date`, active status, normative status, and `abstract=false`. The `baseDefinition` change is real but classified as an inherited/global primitive hierarchy change.
Both snapshots contain the same four element ids: `date`, `date.id`, `date.extension`, and `date.value`. No local element addition, removal, rename, split, merge, or move was found.
Cardinalities are unchanged: root `date` is `0..*`, `date.id` is `0..1`, `date.extension` is `0..*`, and `date.value` is `0..1` in both R4 and R6.
`date.value` remains `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.Date` with the FHIR type extension value `date`. `date.id` remains `System.String` and `date.extension` remains `Extension`.
`date` has no Reference-typed elements or targetProfiles in either version.
`date` has no terminology bindings, so there is no binding strength or value set change to assess.

The computable FHIRPath expressions copied into the `date` snapshot are unchanged for `ele-1` and `ext-1`. R6 removes XPath fields and changes some inherited human-readable constraint text; those are inherited Element/Extension presentation changes and not local `date` validation changes.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value appears on the local `date` elements in either StructureDefinition.

The regex extension on `date.value` is identical in R4 and R6: it permits year, year-month, and full-date forms without a UTC offset, subject to the shared semantic requirement that dates be valid dates.
`isModifier` remains `false` for all `date` snapshot elements in both versions.
`isSummary` remains `false` for all `date` snapshot elements in both versions.
No local slicing definition appears on the `date` snapshot elements in either version.

The definition changes from "There is no time zone" to "There is no UTC offset." This appears to clarify the same lexical rule because the regex and type are unchanged, but the rendered datatype page or official diff would improve confidence about editorial intent.

`date.value` remains represented as an XML attribute and the primitive extension-bearing shape remains represented by `date.id`, `date.extension`, and `date.value`. No local JSON/XML representation change was found in the datatype StructureDefinition.

Because R6 keeps the same `date.value` regex and FHIRPath type, an R6 primitive date value that is valid under the core datatype is representable as an R4 date value. R6-only StructureDefinition metadata, such as type characteristics, is not instance content.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds type-characteristics metadata `has-range` and `has-length` to date
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These are StructureDefinition metadata extensions, not instance elements or lexical constraints on `date.value`. The allowed date string forms, cardinality, and FHIRPath type are unchanged, so existing R4 date instances are not invalidated by this metadata.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-aware code generators or validation tooling may use these characteristics to expose range or length behavior for primitive dates. R4 tooling that does not know these metadata extensions should not treat their absence as a data conversion problem.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Definition now says date has no UTC offset instead of no time zone
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 and R6 regexes are identical and neither permits a timezone or UTC offset suffix. This is best read as a clarification of the same conformance rule rather than a changed value domain.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and tests should continue to distinguish `date` from `dateTime`: a `date` value such as `2026-05-18` has no offset component, and offset-bearing values must be represented with a different datatype where appropriate.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 updates publication metadata without changing the canonical date datatype
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds or updates metadata such as `experimental=false`, jurisdiction, generated narrative, publisher/contact details, workgroup metadata, package version, and FHIR version. These do not alter instance validation for `date`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that diff StructureDefinition metadata may report these changes, but migration logic should separate package/publication metadata from datatype value-domain changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `date` now specializes `PrimitiveType` rather than `Element`. That class-hierarchy shift may matter for generated inheritance models, validators, and cross-version tooling, but it is a shared primitive datatype/base artifact issue and should be assessed in the `PrimitiveType`/`DataType` report rather than as a local `date` finding.

The `date` snapshot shows inherited Element/Extension constraint presentation changes, including removed XPath fields and minor human text changes. The computable expressions are unchanged locally; any cross-version impact should be owned by the base Element/Extension analyses.
